0.content:
MECHANICS AUTHORITY
Core owns universal formulas and resolution procedures.
Content owns concrete Classes, Skills, Gear, creature anchors and other authored mechanics.
Lore owns setting facts and public/world knowledge.
System owns the private player UI and Character Creation flow.
The active host/runtime may store and render mutable state in its own existing presentation.

Avereth defines semantic state and resolved values only. It NEVER requires a host-specific envelope, XML/tag set, Markdown style, block order, or duplicated tracker format.
Resolved mechanics are binding. A specific explicit mechanic overrides a general rule only within its stated scope.
Do not add hidden level multipliers, duplicate stat scaling, narrative bonuses, or other unlisted modifiers.

1.content:
PERSISTENT STATE
Treat the latest valid tracked/explicit authoritative state as the starting point for the next state.
Apply only changes that actually occurred; unchanged Rank, Class, Domain, Skills, Proficiency, Quests, Equipment, Inventory, ammunition, Coin, documents, statuses and other possessions remain unchanged.

Core decides when values change; the active runtime/presentation stores or carries the result. Avereth does not define any host envelope, tag, ordering, Markdown, or rendering rules.

PHYSICAL OWNERSHIP
Nearby, offered, dropped, corpse-held or harvestable objects remain external until a real transfer establishes possession. Spending, firing, consuming, dropping, losing or removing an item likewise requires an established change.

LEVEL/COMBAT DELTA
Combat, Combat End and Level-up never rebuild the sheet from defaults. Start from the last complete state and apply only the resolved deltas.

2.content:
CORE STATS
STR = physical force.
VIT = health and physical resilience.
AGI = speed, reflexes and initiative.
INT = magical power/complexity.
PER = accuracy/precision/crit/detection.
WIL = mana control/mental resistance.

DERIVED FORMULAS
Max HP = 50 + Level×5 + VIT×5
Max MP = INT×8 + WIL×4
Max STA = 100 for normal Human core-stat characters.
Initiative = AGI + floor(PER/2)
Base DEF = floor(VIT/4)
Base MDEF = floor(WIL/4)
Character Crit = 5% + PER/10 percentage points, only for profiles that use Crit.

STAMINA LOCK
Normal Human Max STA does NOT scale with Level, VIT or AGI. It remains 100 unless an explicit species/profile/mechanic says otherwise.
All physical attacks used by Human/core-stat characters must pay their written STA Cost. Physical Basic Attacks use the Content-defined STA Cost.
Generic direct-stat Monsters do not gain STA and their natural attacks remain no-resource unless an explicit authored profile says otherwise.
0 STA creates no universal exhaustion penalty; it only prevents actions whose STA Cost cannot be paid.
There is no automatic in-combat STA regeneration.

TOTAL COMBAT VALUES
ATK = equipped Gear ATK + explicit ATK bonuses.
MATK = equipped Gear MATK + explicit MATK bonuses.
DEF = Base DEF + equipped Gear DEF + explicit DEF bonuses.
MDEF = Base MDEF + equipped Gear MDEF + explicit MDEF bonuses.

CORE STATS NEVER ADD DIRECTLY TO ATK OR MATK unless an explicit mechanic says so. Stat contribution to an attack comes through that action's written Scaling.
There is no derived Movement stat. Combat movement uses the universal Range-Band rules.
There is no passive Evasion score. AGI does not automatically reduce incoming Hit Chance.
Preserve fractional intermediate values; round only where a rule explicitly says to round.

4.content:
CLASS FRAMEWORK
A Class is the character's major power path. Base Class selection may apply a one-time Level-1 growth package defined by Content.

Standard evolution milestones occur every 15 Levels: 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90 unless explicit content says otherwise.
Evolution choices are generated from established development: repeated Skills/elements, weapon style, stat investment, role, training, major victories, discoveries and other meaningful history.

Do not award a specialized or rare evolution from one trivial use. Offer multiple plausible options when history supports them.
Evolution may add or transform passives, permissions, traits, Domains or other explicit mechanics, but it does not silently add universal HP/stat growth beyond rules actually written elsewhere.

Skills remain open-learn unless an explicit prerequisite says otherwise.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

5.comment: [SKILL] Skill Structure, Learning, Proficiency, and Evolution
5.content:
SKILL STRUCTURE
A Skill defines only fields it needs: Rank, Complexity, Tags, Type, Power/scaling, ATK/MATK use, Cost, Range, Hit modifier and explicit Effects.

Rank = broad power band.
Complexity 1/2/3 = foundation / intermediate / advanced mechanical budget inside that Rank.
Proficiency = mastery of that specific Skill.
Class Affinity = learning speed only, not extra damage after learning.

LEARNING
Unknown Skills require a legitimate acquisition path and Learning Progress unless explicitly granted.
Base Learning Progress: C1 100; C2 200; C3 300.
Apply only the single highest applicable Class Affinity multiplier supplied by Content.

PROFICIENCY
Known Skills use P1-P5.
P1: written mechanics.
P2: Cost ×0.95.
P3: Cost ×0.95; attacks +5pp Hit; non-hit primary numeric effect ×1.05 when meaningful.
P4: Cost ×0.925; damaging Modified Power ×1.10; attacks retain +5pp Hit; comparable non-damage effect ×1.10.
P5: Cost ×0.90; damaging Modified Power ×1.15; attacks retain +5pp Hit; comparable non-damage effect ×1.15; Skill becomes evolution-eligible when its other conditions are met.
Milestone modifiers are totals, not cumulative products.

Proficiency Progress per promotion: C1 75; C2 100; C3 150.
Meaningful use/training may grant progress; trivial safe repetition grants 0.

SKILL EVOLUTION
P5 permits but does not guarantee evolution. The evolved Skill should follow how it was actually used/trained and remain recognizably descended from the prior technique unless a true transformation is established.

Numerical design of new Skills belongs to Content's Skill Design Rules, not Core.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

6.content:
GEAR — v0.1 SIMPLIFIED MODEL:
Normal equipment does NOT modify STR, VIT, AGI, INT, PER, or WIL.

Gear contributes direct combat values only:
ATK = physical offensive equipment power
MATK = magical offensive equipment power
DEF = physical defensive equipment power added to Base DEF
MDEF = magical defensive equipment power added to Base MDEF

Typical use:
- physical weapons primarily grant ATK
- magical foci/staves primarily grant MATK
- armor grants DEF and/or MDEF
- accessories may grant any of ATK, MATK, DEF, or MDEF

Add equipped Gear ATK/MATK/DEF/MDEF directly to the character's derived combat values. Gear never requires recalculating Core Stats.

Special item effects may later grant explicit modifiers such as Fire Damage +10%, Crit +3 percentage points, or Mana Cost -5%, but only when written on the item. Do not translate ordinary gear into hidden Core Stat bonuses.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

7.comment: [CHECK] Check Gate and Universal Check Resolution
7.content:
CHECK GATE:
Do not roll merely because an action exists. Use a mechanical check only when BOTH are true:
1. the outcome is genuinely uncertain, and
2. success or failure has meaningful consequences.

Do NOT roll for routine actions, ordinary conversation, obvious observations, uncomplicated walking/travel, scene transitions, basic searches where nothing is concealed, or other low-stakes actions with no meaningful uncertainty.

CHECK TYPES:
1. Automatic: no roll when the result is obvious, uncontested, or effectively trivial.
2. Difficulty Check: Actor Score versus a fixed Difficulty Score.
3. Opposed Check: Actor Score versus another creature/effect's Opposition Score.

SCORES:
Actor Score = relevant Core Stat + explicit Skill/Technique bonus + explicit effect bonuses.
Opposition Score = relevant opposing Stat/Difficulty + explicit opposing Skill/Technique bonus + explicit effect bonuses.
Do not assume raw Skill Proficiency equals a check bonus unless that Skill explicitly converts proficiency into one.

SUCCESS CHANCE:
Chance% = Actor Score ÷ (Actor Score + Opposition Score) × 100.
Roll one d100. A roll less than or equal to Chance% succeeds.

If the power gap is so extreme that the outcome is effectively trivial, use Automatic resolution instead of forcing an artificial 1-in-20 style failure/success chance.

The Narrator may choose the relevant stat/skill from the actual attempted action, but must not choose whichever stat gives the desired story outcome.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

8.content:
SITUATIONAL MODIFIERS:
Translate established circumstances into a small standardized modifier to the relevant Actor or Opposition Score.

Minor advantage/disadvantage: ±10%
Strong advantage/disadvantage: ±20%
Extreme advantage/disadvantage: ±35%

Multiple independent modifiers on the same side add before multiplication.
Example: Detection Score 30, daylight +10% and very quiet surroundings +10% => 30 × 1.20 = 36.

Do not invent arbitrary percentages. Use only modifiers justified by concrete circumstances.

STEALTH VS DETECTION:
Typical Stealth Score = AGI + explicit Stealth bonus.
Typical Detection Score = PER + explicit Awareness/Detection bonus.
Then apply situational modifiers and resolve as an Opposed Check.

Examples of context:
- bright daylight may aid Detection
- darkness/cover may aid Stealth
- very quiet surroundings may aid Detection
- heavy rain/crowd noise may hinder Detection
- rushing may hinder Stealth
- deliberate slow movement may aid Stealth when circumstances permit

PERCEPTION IS NOT OMNISCIENCE:
A successful perception, insight, tracking, or deception-related check reveals only evidence actually available through that action. It does not reveal hidden thoughts, System information, exact stats, secret skill names, narrator knowledge, or the objectively true explanation without evidence.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

9.content:
RANDOM RESOLUTION
When a rule requires randomness, use exactly the roll(s) required by that mechanic.

Standard checks, hit checks, and critical checks use d100 unless a specific mechanic says otherwise.
Damage variance uses one random multiplier from 0.90 to 1.10 inclusive.

Use an available external dice/random source when one is active. If no external random source exists, generate one value for the required roll and treat it as binding.

ROLL LOCK
A required roll is generated exactly once for that resolution step.
Validation/audit passes NEVER reroll, replace, improve, worsen, or sample a second value. They recompute the formula using the already-fixed roll/variance.

Never fudge or ignore a valid result because a different result would make a better story. Never invent an unnecessary attempted action merely to consume a supplied die result.

rpg_compile.mode: condensed: RNG LOCK / audit never rerolls

10.content:
ATTACK HIT CHECK
Use a hit check only when the attack can meaningfully miss. A helpless target or an unavoidable established effect does not require a fake hit roll.

CHARACTER / CORE-STAT BASE HIT
For combatants using Core Stats:
Base Hit Chance% = 70 + (PER × 0.50).

DIRECT-STAT MONSTER BASE HIT
If a fixed Monster profile supplies a direct Hit value, that value IS its Base Hit Chance.
Do NOT apply the Human/Core-Stat formula, invent PER, or add 70 again.

FINAL HIT CHANCE
Final Hit Chance% = applicable Base Hit Chance
+ explicit attack/Skill Hit Modifier
+ explicit attacker bonuses
- explicit defender avoidance penalties
+/- established situational modifiers.

Clamp a genuinely uncertain Hit Chance to 20%-95%.
Roll one d100. Roll <= Final Hit Chance hits.

There is no passive Evasion score and no default defender-stat subtraction.
AGI does not automatically reduce an enemy's Hit Chance.

DEFENSIVE AVOIDANCE
Explicit dodge, deflection, concealment, displacement or similar effects may impose a direct percentage-point penalty on incoming Hit Chance.

AUTOMATIC-HIT LIMIT
An active mobile combatant is meaningfully missable by default. Close range, large size, weak Rank, low HP, a charge, or expected narrative success does NOT create an automatic hit.
Skip the Hit roll only for a genuinely helpless/immobile target, an established unavoidable effect, or an explicit mechanic.

DIRECT-PROFILE LOCK
Once Combat START fixes a Monster's Hit value, do not replace it with a newly invented value, Core Stat conversion, appearance-based bonus, or later narration.

11.comment: [COMBAT] Damage, Defense, Resistance, Variance, and Criticals
11.content:
DAMAGE PIPELINE
Use the attack's explicit damage type and scaling. Do not apply both physical and magical equipment power unless the attack explicitly says so.

CHARACTER PHYSICAL RAW POWER
Raw Power = Skill Base + explicit Stat Scaling + ATK.

CHARACTER MAGICAL RAW POWER
Raw Power = Skill Base + explicit Stat Scaling + MATK.

DIRECT-STAT MONSTER NATURAL ATTACK
For a Monster profile whose natural attack uses direct ATK:
Raw Power = profile ATK.
Do NOT add ATK a second time, invent STR/VIT scaling, or convert the Monster to Human Core Stats.
If an authored Monster attack explicitly defines another Power formula, use that formula instead.

HYBRID / SPECIAL
A hybrid or authored special attack explicitly defines its coefficients, ATK/MATK use, defense and exceptions.

CENTRAL DAMAGE ORDER
Unless an explicit mechanic says otherwise:
1. Raw Power.
2. Explicit attack/Skill Power modifiers.
3. Applicable Skill Proficiency Power modifier.
4. Other explicit attacker buffs/debuffs and tactical Power modifiers.
5. Domain / Authority Power modifiers.
6. Explicit Defense Penetration or Defense reduction.
7. Defense: max(Modified Power - applicable DEF/MDEF, Modified Power ×0.10).
8. Resistance / Weakness.
9. Damage Variance ×0.90-1.10.
10. Critical Damage, default ×1.50, only if the profile/attack uses Crit.
11. Explicit Final Damage modifiers/reductions.
12. Round ONCE to nearest whole number; minimum 1 if positive damage remains.
13. Applicable Barrier absorbs damage.
14. Remaining damage reduces HP.

PRECISION LOCK
Keep all intermediate values at full precision.
NEVER round an individual Stat-scaling term.
NEVER round the sum of multiple scaling terms.
NEVER round Raw Power, Modified Power, defense result, resistance result, variance result or critical result before step 12.
Decimals are valid authoritative intermediate values. Round only the final positive damage at step 12.

DEFENSE
Physical attacks normally use DEF. Magical attacks normally use MDEF.
After Defense = max(Modified Power - Defense, Modified Power ×0.10).
The 10% floor does not bypass explicit Immunity/invulnerability.

RESISTANCE
Standard applicable Resistance reduces the applicable damage/effect to 50% unless explicit content says otherwise.
For duration-only effects, halve duration and round up unless the effect says otherwise.
Do not stack duplicate instances of the same standard Resistance unless explicitly allowed.

WEAKNESS
A Weakness increases an applicable effect only when explicit content defines the increase. There is no universal Weakness multiplier.

IMMUNITY
Applicable Immunity reduces that damage/effect to 0 unless an explicit bypass exists.

VARIANCE
After Defense and Resistance/Weakness, apply one random multiplier from 0.90 to 1.10.

CRITICALS
For combatants using the Character Crit model:
Base Crit Chance = 5% + (PER ÷10) percentage points. No cap on the PER-derived portion is defined; do not invent one.
Default Critical Damage = ×1.50.

DIRECT-STAT MONSTER CRIT LOCK
Generic direct-stat Monsters have Crit:none by default.
Do not roll Crit for them unless their fixed authored profile explicitly says they use Crit.

FINAL DAMAGE / HP
Apply explicit Final Damage modifiers after Crit unless their timing says otherwise.
Round once at the end, then Barrier, then HP. HP cannot fall below 0.

DEATH
0 HP = dead. There is no universal dying/unconscious/death-save state.
A dead target cannot act or receive ordinary healing; only explicit resurrection/revival can reverse death.

WORKED PRECISION EXAMPLES
17.5 Raw vs DEF2, variance0.94: (17.5-2)×0.94 = 14.57 -> 15.
12.25 Raw vs DEF2, variance1.08, Crit×1.5: (12.25-2)×1.08×1.5 = 16.605 -> 17.

POSITIVE-HP ACTION LOCK
At 1+ HP a combatant remains alive and able to take its normal Turn unless an explicit status, restraint, surrender, injury mechanic or other rule says otherwise.
Narrative blood/wounds, low HP or dramatic prose do not independently create action loss, helplessness, immobility or penalties.

rpg_compile.mode: condensed: PRECISION LOCK, turn step 9 DAMAGE

12.comment: [COMBAT] Multi-Hit, Range Bands, Positioning, and Tactical Modifiers
12.content:
MULTI-HIT SKILLS
Each strike of a multi-hit Skill resolves separately when the Skill says so.
The Skill defines each strike's power, Hit modifier, targeting, and equipment contribution.

Unless the Skill explicitly says otherwise:
- each strike makes its own Hit roll,
- each successful strike makes its own Crit roll,
- each strike resolves defense/resistance separately.

There is NO universal 1.00 / 0.75 / 0.50 multi-attack penalty.
Do not import one from another game unless a specific Skill defines it.

Stop resolving additional strikes against a target once that target is dead unless the Skill explicitly retargets, continues through the target, or has an area effect.

AREA-OF-EFFECT ATTACKS
An AoE attack uses ONE shared Hit roll for the entire AoE unless the Skill explicitly says it automatically hits or resolves separately.

If the shared Hit roll succeeds, all valid targets in the AoE are hit.
If it fails, all valid targets in the AoE are missed.

After a successful shared Hit roll, make ONE shared Crit roll for the AoE.
If it Crits, all targets successfully hit by that AoE take the Skill's normal Critical Damage.
Even with shared Hit/Crit rolls, each target resolves its own DEF/MDEF, Resistance, Immunity, Final Damage modifiers, Barrier and HP separately.

RANGE BANDS — NO METER TRACKING
Combat uses only four mechanical relative Range Bands:
ENGAGED < SHORT < MEDIUM < LONG.

ENGAGED = immediate contact/melee reach.
SHORT = one normal combat movement from ENGAGED.
MEDIUM = two normal combat movements from ENGAGED.
LONG = three normal combat movements from ENGAGED.

Anything clearly farther away than LONG is outside ordinary combat range until fiction/movement brings it into LONG.
Do NOT maintain exact combat distance in meters/feet/yards.
If prior narration contains an exact distance, convert it once to the most reasonable Range Band from the established scene, then track the band only.
Do not infer a hidden exact meter value from a Range Band.
Ordinal form: ENGAGED=0, SHORT=1, MEDIUM=2, LONG=3. An action may target band b only if b <= its listed band; one normal movement changes the band by at most 1.

ACTION RANGE — LISTED BAND IS THE MAXIMUM RANGE
ENGAGED can target ENGAGED only.
SHORT can target ENGAGED or SHORT.
MEDIUM can target ENGAGED, SHORT or MEDIUM.
LONG can target ENGAGED, SHORT, MEDIUM or LONG.
A Ranged action is not automatically penalized merely because the target is ENGAGED unless an explicit rule says so.
Never reinterpret a listed Range Band as a minimum range.

NORMAL COMBAT MOVEMENT — ADJACENCY LOCK
There is no Movement stat.
Every normal combatant may shift by at most ONE ADJACENT Range Band during its own normal Turn, toward or away from a plausible target/direction, plus take one Main Action.
The only ordinary one-band transitions are:
ENGAGED <-> SHORT
SHORT <-> MEDIUM
MEDIUM <-> LONG
Normal movement NEVER jumps MEDIUM -> ENGAGED, LONG -> SHORT, or any other two-band step.
Movement and Main Action may occur in either sensible order.
Thus from ENGAGED, three normal Turns of uninterrupted movement can reach LONG: ENGAGED -> SHORT -> MEDIUM -> LONG.
Narrative words such as sprint, rush, charge, pounce or flee do not grant extra band shifts by themselves.
Only an explicit Skill/Trait/status/environmental rule may grant, prevent or alter a band shift.

PAIRWISE RANGE STATE
Track only Range Bands that matter mechanically between relevant combatants/positions.
Do not force a full geometric grid.
When movement affects several combatants, update only relationships logically changed by the established direction/formation.
Never manipulate an NPC's movement merely to preserve or invalidate a pending player action.

LINE OF SIGHT
Direct attacks and direct-target Skills normally require a clear line of sight unless the Skill explicitly bypasses it.

Full obstruction / Full Cover:
- no valid direct line of sight,
- the target cannot be selected by a normal direct attack through that obstruction.

Partial Cover:
- line of sight still exists,
- attacks against that target suffer -20 percentage points Hit Chance.

Do not create additional cover grades unless later content explicitly defines them.

FORCED MOVEMENT
A mechanical forced-movement effect must state the band shift it causes.
When an unwilling target is pushed/pulled and no explicit resistance rule exists, use a normal Opposed Check:
- physical source force: source STR,
- spell-driven force: source INT,
- another explicit force may use another stat only when the effect says so,
versus target STR by default.

If the source wins, apply the effect's stated band shift.
If it fails, no forced band shift occurs.
Solid obstacles can stop displacement.
Do not invent collision damage merely because movement is blocked.

TACTICAL ADVANTAGE
Concrete positioning may justify standardized Hit Chance modifiers.

Default attack Hit Chance modifiers:
Minor advantage/disadvantage: ±10 percentage points.
Strong advantage/disadvantage: ±20 percentage points.
Extreme advantage/disadvantage: ±35 percentage points.

Partial Cover has its specific -20 percentage-point Hit rule above.
These combat Hit modifiers are separate from percentage-based Actor/Opposition Score modifiers used by generic non-combat Checks.

For damage, apply a tactical damage multiplier only when a rule, Skill, or clearly established combat circumstance explicitly justifies it:
+10%, +20%, or +35%.

AMBUSH EXCEPTION
Ambush itself does NOT grant a direct tactical Damage multiplier.
Use the dedicated Ambush rules:
- one Opening Action on a successful true Ambush,
- +25 percentage points Crit Chance for eligible attacks in that Opening Action,
- then normal Initiative.
Do not add an automatic Ambush Hit or Damage bonus.

RANGE / MOVEMENT GATE
At attack resolution, the target must be inside the action's locked Range Band after only legal band movement.
If legal movement cannot bring the target into range, that attack is illegal.
Never compress or reinterpret range narratively to force an attack to happen.

rpg_compile.mode: condensed: RANGE CORE, turn step 5, combat detail

13.content:
STATUS EFFECTS:
Mechanical status effects are explicit game state, not decorative narration.

A status should define as applicable:
- Name
- Source
- Magnitude/Tier
- Duration or removal condition
- Mechanical effect
- Stacking rule if stacking is explicitly allowed

Examples may include Burning, Bleeding, Poisoned, Slowed, Stunned, Silenced, Crippled, Off-Balance, Weakened, Empowered, Frozen, or other content-defined effects.

Do not invent a mechanical status merely because narration mentions pain, sparks, blood, fear, cold, or similar flavor.
Likewise, when a resolved mechanic applies a status, narration should reflect it.

DEFAULT NON-STACKING RULE:
The same named status/effect does NOT stack its magnitude by default.

Examples:
- two Bleeds do not deal double Bleed damage,
- two Slows do not automatically add together,
- two identical DEF reductions do not automatically sum.

A Class Passive, Skill, Domain Law, Trait, or other explicit mechanic may create an exception and allow stacking.

REAPPLICATION OF THE SAME EFFECT:
A valid reapplication may extend the remaining duration, but does not increase the effect magnitude merely because it was applied again.

Default duration extension:
remaining duration + the newly applied listed duration.

If the new application has a stronger magnitude than the existing same-named effect:
use the stronger magnitude while keeping the extended duration.

If an explicit effect says it refreshes rather than extends, follow that effect instead.

DIFFERENT EFFECTS:
Different named effects may coexist simultaneously.
Each tracks its own magnitude, duration, source, and removal condition independently.

TURN-BASED DURATION:
Unless an effect explicitly states another timing, a duration measured in Turns is anchored to the Turn on which the source applied/activated it.

One Turn of duration means:
from the moment the effect is applied until the start of that source's next normal Turn.

Two Turns means:
until the start of that source's second subsequent normal Turn.

And so on.

The Opening Action from an Ambush is not a normal Turn for duration counting unless an effect explicitly says otherwise.

PERIODIC EFFECTS:
A periodic effect such as Bleeding or Burning must state when its periodic effect resolves, for example:
- at the start of the affected target's Turn,
- at the end of the affected target's Turn,
- or another explicit trigger.

Duration tracking and periodic-trigger timing are separate.
Do not invent additional ticks because duration was extended.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

14.content:
INJURIES:
HP and physical injuries are related but not identical.
A mechanically significant injury may persist after HP is restored when the resolved event or explicit injury rule supports it.

Do not create broken bones, severed limbs, organ damage, permanent disability, or similar major injury from minor damage solely for dramatic prose.
Severe injuries require a sufficiently severe resolved event, explicit Skill/status effect, or later dedicated injury rule.

DEATH:
0 HP = dead.
There is no universal unconscious/dying state at 0 HP in the current Core.

HEALING:
Healing Skills and effects use their explicit formulas and targets.
Healing may restore HP, remove/reduce a status, treat an injury, or do several of these only when the effect explicitly says so.

NO OVERHEALING:
Current HP cannot exceed Max HP through ordinary healing.
Any healing beyond Max HP is lost unless an explicit mechanic converts excess healing into another effect.

Ordinary healing cannot affect a dead target.
Resurrection/revival requires an explicit mechanic.

Restoring HP does not automatically erase every injury or status.
Treat each tracked effect according to its own rule.

NATURAL RECOVERY:
Natural HP, MP, and STA recovery occurs only outside active combat.

There is no universal fixed natural-regeneration rate in the current Core.
Outside combat, the Narrator determines reasonable recovery from rest and elapsed time while respecting established injuries, exhaustion, circumstances, and later content.

IN-COMBAT RECOVERY:
Do not grant natural HP/MP/STA regeneration during active combat.

Combat recovery occurs only through an explicit source such as:
- potion/consumable,
- healing or recovery Skill,
- spell,
- buff,
- Class effect,
- Domain effect,
- another explicit mechanic.

A scene transition alone does not silently restore resources.

NARRATIVE-WOUND LOCK:
Narration may describe cuts, bites, bruising, soreness, blood, or other visible consequences supported by the resolved damage. Such prose is descriptive only unless an explicit mechanic creates a Condition/Status/Injury effect.

Do not convert ordinary damage into a mechanical Active Effect, Range-Band movement penalty, Hit penalty, action loss, grapple, immobilization, ongoing damage, or other rules effect merely because the prose describes a wound. If a descriptive wound is mirrored in a tracker, mark/understand it as descriptive and mechanically inert unless a defined rule says otherwise.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

15.comment: [POWER] Barriers, Counters, Dispels, Interrupts, and Power-vs-Power
15.content:
POWER-VS-POWER INTERACTIONS:
When two powers directly contest each other and no specific rule already resolves the interaction, use the Universal Opposed Check framework with mechanically relevant scores.

Examples:
- Dispel Power vs effect stability/resistance
- Interrupt Power vs channel/concentration resistance
- Grapple/hold vs escape resistance
- concealment vs detection
- control effect vs WIL or another explicit resistance

BARRIERS:
A barrier with its own Barrier HP absorbs applicable resolved Final Damage after the attack's normal damage calculation and before the protected target loses HP. Subtract damage from Barrier HP. Excess damage carries through only when the barrier rule allows it or when damage exceeds remaining Barrier HP.

PENETRATION:
If a skill has explicit Barrier Penetration or Defense Penetration, apply exactly that percentage or flat value. Do not infer penetration merely because an attack sounds sharp, spatial, powerful, or precise.

COUNTERS/PARRIES:
A counter, parry, deflection, reflection, or reaction occurs only when a skill/trait or established combat option permits it. Resolve it using its own stated mechanic rather than giving free reactions for dramatic convenience.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

16.content:
ELEMENTS AND THE WORLD:
Powers interact with the physical environment. The Narrator establishes factual conditions such as rain, darkness, standing water, dry brush, stone walls, smoke, strong wind, confined space, or conductive metal. Mechanics then apply only justified interactions.

Useful interaction tags include:
WET; BURNING; FROZEN; CONDUCTIVE; OBSCURED; BRITTLE; UNSTABLE.
Content may define additional tags.

A tag does not automatically create a huge damage multiplier. When no specific skill interaction exists, use at most the standard situational modifier tiers (±10%, ±20%, ±35%) to the score or effect that the environment actually changes.

Examples of principle, not automatic universal bonuses:
- WET conditions can make electrical conduction easier when the lightning effect can use that pathway.
- abundant water can make water manipulation easier; very dry conditions can make creating/gathering water harder.
- fire can ignite genuinely flammable material and can be harder to sustain in conditions that realistically suppress flame.
- cold/ice may freeze available water when sufficient power and time are present.

Do not invent impossible elemental knowledge or effects solely because two element names appear together. Specific Skills and established world rules take priority.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

17.comment: [POWER] Detection, Appraisal, Mana Sense, and Information Limits
17.content:
POWER DETECTION:
A detection or appraisal ability reveals only what its explicit scope permits.

Seeing an unfamiliar ability does not automatically reveal its name, class, exact stats, mana cost, cooldown, hidden traits, limitations, source, rarity, or counters.

A basic Mana Sense may reveal facts such as presence, approximate intensity, direction, or an obvious elemental nature only when its skill definition permits those observations.

Exact mechanical information requires an ability that explicitly provides exact information.

A successful detection/appraisal check does not override secrecy, player-only System information, or NPC knowledge boundaries. The result becomes knowledge only for the character who actually performed or received that detection.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

18.content:
DELIBERATE NON-DEFINITIONS:
The following are intentionally NOT hard-coded in this Core file:
- concrete Classes, class growth, Skills, starter kits, creature anchors and Gear values (Content owns them)
- the Character Creation flow and starting possessions (System and First Message own them)
- a universal multi-action combat turn beyond one normal one-band movement + 1 Main Action
- detailed injury thresholds
- fixed numerical out-of-combat natural-regeneration rates
- universal fall/collision damage tables
- detailed resurrection rules
- loot tables, fixed prices, quest rewards other than Quest XP, Guild progression, crafting, or world lore

Core defines the XP threshold curve, the Combat XP Formula with locked DefeatXP, and Quest XP. Rewards for discoveries, achievements or other sources belong to later content/reward modules.

When an intentionally open subsystem is needed, use the appropriate later module/content definition.
Do not silently import rules from Obsidian Summoner, Aethermere, D&D, or another RPG simply because this Core leaves that subsystem open.

19.content:
DOMAIN MECHANICS — FIRST TRANSCENDENT / B-RANK LAYER

A Domain is a class- or creature-bound active authority field.
It is NOT an ordinary open-learn Skill and is NOT a passive once unlocked.

DOMAIN ACTIVATION:
- A Domain is inactive by default.
- Its owner consciously activates it like a special Skill/ability.
- Activation costs no MP, STA, or other normal resource.
- Activation does not consume the normal Main Action; it is a special Domain Activation that may be used once at the start of the owner's turn.
- The owner may voluntarily dismiss the Domain.
- Only one personal Domain may normally be active at a time.
- A Domain normally collapses when its owner is incapacitated.
- Domain activation has no Skill Proficiency and no Complexity progression unless later content explicitly defines Domain-specific mastery.

NASCENT B-RANK DOMAIN:
The standard first Domain is a Nascent Domain.
Default player reach = SHORT Range Band around the owner and moving with the owner.
Specific content may explicitly alter the Domain's Range Band.

UNIVERSAL LOWER-RANK SUPPRESSION:
While a B-rank Domain is active, a target below B-rank that lacks an equivalent Domain/Authority is qualitatively suppressed.

For a lower-rank creature inside the Domain:
- outgoing Modified Power ×0.65
- Hit Chance -15 percentage points
- the Domain owner gains ×1.20 outgoing Modified Power against that creature
- the Domain owner gains +15 percentage points Hit Chance against that creature

A lower-rank attack, projectile, spell, or other hostile effect created outside the Domain but entering the Domain to affect its owner is also subject to the ×0.65 Modified Power and -15 percentage-point Hit penalties where mechanically applicable.

Apply these Domain modifiers after the Skill's normal written power, Proficiency modifiers, and ordinary tactical modifiers, but before defense/resistance and final variance.

DOMAIN CLASH — SAME RANK:
When two B-rank Domain users oppose one another with active Domains, the universal lower-rank suppression does not apply between those B-rank users.
Their individual Domain Laws remain active according to their own text.
Do not invent an automatic 'stronger Domain wins' score in this version.

LOWER-RANK INTERACTION:
A lower-rank character cannot normally dispel, cancel, overwrite, or contest a B-rank Domain through ordinary lower-rank Skills.
An explicit Domain-countering, Authority, artifact, narrative exception, or later system rule may override this.

DOMAIN LAW:
Each evolved player Domain has a specific Law derived from the character's previous Class Passive and development path.
The Law is active only while the Domain is active.
The former passive is replaced by this controllable Domain Law rather than stacking separately.

Do not treat Half-Divine/B-rank status as a hidden universal stat multiplier.
Its qualitative advantage is represented by explicit B-rank growth, Gear/Skills, and the Domain rules above.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

20.content:
LOOT RESOLUTION

Loot is physical world state.
Victory makes recoverable loot available; it does NOT automatically teleport loot into Inventory.

The player must actually take, receive, harvest, or otherwise acquire an item before the Tracker adds it to Inventory.

NON-HUMAN MONSTERS / NATIVE FAUNA:
Native fauna and other non-human Monsters normally carry no currency.
Their ordinary loot is made from physically or magically recoverable body/material profiles defined by Content. Faunal Monsters may yield ordinary physical materials such as hide, teeth, antlers/tusks, claws, meat, fat, bone or organs as appropriate.

Examples include:
- hide/pelt,
- fangs,
- claws,
- horns,
- tusks,
- scales,
- bone,
- glands,
- venom,
- spirit essence,
- other species-specific materials.

The condition of the body matters.
A destroyed horn cannot also be recovered intact.
Fire, disintegration, acid, crushing, or other combat consequences may damage or ruin materials.

Monster materials normally carry the same Rank as the defeated monster unless Content explicitly defines an exceptional material.

HUMANS:
Humans grant XP exactly like monsters, but ordinary Human loot is different.

A defeated Human may leave only what they were actually carrying or wearing:
- Copper/Silver/Gold,
- equipped weapon,
- equipped armor,
- equipped accessories,
- consumables,
- documents,
- keys,
- carried valuables,
- other established possessions.

Human currency is contextual, not generated by Rank.
A poor high-rank Human may carry little money; a wealthy low-rank Human may carry more.

GEAR PERSISTENCE:
Looted Gear is the same item instance the defeated owner used.
Preserve its Rank, ATK/MATK/DEF/MDEF, explicit effects, damage state, and identity.
Do not reroll or improve an item merely because it became loot.

A Human's learned Skills do not become loot.
A Skill Stone, manual, or similar Skill item is loot only if it physically existed in that person's possessions.

INTELLIGENT MONSTERS:
If Content or established story state says an intelligent monster carried Gear, currency, documents, or other possessions, those physical possessions may also be recoverable.
Do not invent carried valuables after defeat merely to increase rewards.



OFFICIAL COMBAT-END LOOT TIMING:
When an ACTIVE encounter ends, the [COMBAT END] protocol owns standard reward/loot resolution. It identifies what is physically recoverable before ordinary story play resumes. This creates availability only; ownership still requires an actual take/receive/harvest action. Items physically manipulated during combat remain governed by ordinary state/ownership rules and are not duplicated at Combat End.

REWARD RESOLUTION ORDER:
1. remain in ACTIVE Combat while any hostile combatant remains active; defeated opponents only accumulate Pending Combat XP;
2. at terminal COMBAT END, finalize all Defeated/Escaped opponents and verify Pending Combat XP once;
3. award the verified Pending Combat XP exactly once and resolve all Core Level-ups with carryover;
4. identify physically recoverable loot;
5. narrate what is available;
6. add only items/currency the player actually takes or receives to persistent state.

Do not silently convert monster materials into Gold.
Sale is a separate economic transaction.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

21.content:
PHYSICAL AMMUNITION

Bows require physical arrows.

- A bow attack consumes the number of arrows it explicitly fires, as listed in the action's Ammo field in Content.
- A normal single-projectile bow attack consumes 1 arrow.
- Twin Shot consumes 2 arrows (its Content Ammo field).
- Ammunition is committed exactly once together with the action's Cost, only after the action passed full legality. An illegal or unaffordable action consumes no ammunition.
- If the character lacks enough arrows for the declared attack, that attack cannot be performed: no Cost, ammunition, roll or Turn advance.
- Track remaining arrows as physical Inventory state.
- Ordinary arrows add no bonus damage, accuracy, status, Rank, or other modifier.
- Magical projectiles (for example a Mage Basic Attack or Arcane Bolt) use no physical ammunition unless their action lists Ammo.
- Special ammunition may exist later only when Content explicitly defines it.
- A future Skill that represents an unusual number of projectiles should state its ammunition use explicitly rather than inventing a hidden damage or ammo rule.

22.content:
COIN TRANSACTIONS AND NORMALIZATION

Currency denomination ratios are setting facts from Lore. Under the current Avereth standard:
10 Copper = 1 Silver
10 Silver = 1 Gold
100 Copper = 1 Gold

For every monetary transaction that changes tracked Coin:
1. preserve the exact price already established by Lore, narration, contract, shop, quest, or prior state unless a legitimate in-world cause explicitly changes that price;
2. convert both the character's tracked Coin and the exact transaction amount to total Copper;
3. add or subtract the exact Copper value;
4. reject the transaction if the resulting total would be negative unless an explicit debt/credit rule is established;
5. normalize the remaining total back to Gold, Silver, and Copper using the ratios above;
6. update the tracker to that normalized result.

Example: 5 Silver = 50 Copper. Paying a 10-Copper fee leaves 40 Copper = 4 Silver exactly. No change is owed.

COIN INTEGRITY:
- Coin counts are whole integers. Do not create fractional Copper unless Lore explicitly introduces a smaller denomination.
- Do not invent change that the arithmetic does not produce.
- Do not silently alter an established fee to make a transaction work.
- A denomination mismatch may matter physically (for example, a 2-Copper toll when only Silver is carried). If exact change or exchange availability matters, resolve that as an in-world transaction; never fake the arithmetic.
- If narration, an NPC dossier, or a tracker contains an obvious arithmetic contradiction, the established denomination rules and exact transaction history control the corrected Coin total. Do not preserve an arithmetic error merely because it appeared earlier.

TRACKER REPAIR / NET-HOLDINGS RULE:
- The Coin tracker stores final net holdings after the entire exchange, not the previous tracker total plus received change.
- Change is part of the same transaction; it is not additional income.
- If the previous tracker conflicts with exact established transaction history, reconstruct the correct total from the last reliable holdings plus all established transactions, then write the corrected normalized total.
- Do not propagate a known arithmetic error merely because it is the most recent Character Sheet value.

WHOLE-COPPER PRICE RULE:
Every ordinary price, fee, wage, bounty, or reward must resolve to a whole-Copper amount under the active currency standard. Do not quote a fractional denomination that implies fractional Copper. Under 10 Copper = 1 Silver, "one quarter Silver" (=2.5 Copper) is invalid unless Lore later introduces a smaller denomination.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

23.comment: [COMBAT GATE] Hostile Commitment and Phase State
23.content:
COMBAT PHASE GATE — HOSTILE COMMITMENT ONLY
Combat state is INACTIVE, PENDING, ACTIVE, or TERMINAL/ENDING.

INACTIVE does NOT become Combat merely because danger exists. The following remain INACTIVE by themselves:
- hunting/searching/tracking/following tracks;
- discovering or watching a Monster;
- mutual awareness, growling, territorial display, warning posture or threat;
- stalking, cautious approach/retreat;
- drawing/equipping/holding a weapon ready;
- aiming alone without actually declaring an attack.

HOSTILE COMMITMENT exists only when an immediate harmful action is actually committed:
1. Alaric declares a damaging/offensive attack or Skill against an unwilling target;
2. an NPC/Monster begins an actual immediate attack whose purpose is to strike now;
3. a true ambush attack begins;
4. a damaging trap/hazard is deliberately activated against a target.

VISIBLE TRIGGER ACTION
A visible non-ambush trigger action is PENDING until Initiative is fixed. It never resolves before Turn Order merely because it started the encounter.
A successful true Ambush uses the dedicated Opening Action rule.

SOLE-HOSTILE TARGET DEFAULT
If exactly ONE valid hostile target exists when Alaric declares an offensive action without naming a target, that sole hostile may be used automatically.
If TWO OR MORE valid hostile targets exist and the action requires a target, do not choose among them for Alaric. Stop before cost/ammo/RNG/effect until Alaric specifies the target.

AUTONOMOUS NPC START — DATA SAFETY
If an NPC/Monster becomes hostily committed in a generation where complete Combat Initialization rules/data are not available, do NOT improvise the attack outcome.
Freeze at the commitment boundary, persist the encounter as PENDING, record participants + relevant Range Bands + triggering action, and resolve it through normal Initialization on the next mechanical pass.
Player input cannot erase or jump ahead of that pending commitment.
The same data safety applies when an attack Alaric declares starts a NEW encounter in a generation where complete Combat Initialization rules/data are not available: never improvise its outcome; persist it as the PENDING triggering action. An encounter that is already ACTIVE is never re-frozen this way.

PHASE MARKER CONTRACT
Persistent encounter state must make exactly one semantic phase recoverable: PENDING, ACTIVE, or INACTIVE.
A host may render that semantic state in its own existing wording/decoration. Avereth does not prescribe punctuation, Markdown, tags, envelope, or ordering.
Runtime trigger logic should tolerate harmless host decoration around the Combat label rather than requiring one exact visual string.

NO PREMATURE COMBAT STATE
While INACTIVE, do not create Round, Current Actor, Turn Order, Pending Combat XP, or a locked combat profile solely because violence might happen.

rpg_compile.mode: condensed: COMBAT GATE, PHASE, START FALLBACK

24.content:
ROUNDS / TURNS / INITIATIVE
Combat ACTIVE uses fixed Initiative and a fixed Turn Order unless an explicit effect changes Initiative.

INITIATIVE
Core-stat combatant: Initiative = AGI + floor(PER/2).
Direct-stat Monster: use locked profile Initiative directly.
Tie: higher PER when both profiles possess PER; otherwise resolve the tie once without bias and lock it.

NORMAL TURN
Each living active combatant normally receives one Turn per Round:
- one normal shift to an ADJACENT Range Band;
- one Main Action;
- movement/Main Action may occur in either sensible order.
Explicit Skills/effects may modify this.
Ordinary movement cannot skip a Range Band.

CURRENT ACTOR LOCK
Only Current Actor resolves a Turn.
A user combat message authorizes/queues Alaric's declared action for Alaric's next legal Turn; it never changes Turn Order.
NPC/Monster Turns resolve automatically until Alaric becomes Current Actor or Combat ends.

PENDING TRIGGER ACTION
On visible Combat start, the triggering hostile action remains Pending.
When its actor receives the first legal Turn, resolve that exact action if it remains legal.
If an earlier actor's legitimate action changes range/LoS/resources/state so Alaric's pending action is no longer legal, do not bend the earlier action or substitute a replacement. Stop at Alaric's decision boundary with no cost/ammo/RNG for the now-illegal action.

POSITIVE HP LOCK
At 1+ HP a combatant receives its normal Turn unless an explicit status/restraint/surrender/injury mechanic says otherwise.
Low HP, blood, pain prose or dramatic momentum never skip a Turn.

AMBUSH
A true Ambush requires the target to be genuinely unaware of the attacker/attack until commitment.
Unawareness, concealment or favorable position must rest on established facts or actions the user actually declared; a posture, hiding place or stealth approach the narrator invented for Alaric never creates an Ambush or any other mechanical advantage.
On success, attacker gets one Opening Action before Round 1.
Eligible attack in that Opening Action gains +25 percentage points Crit Chance.
Then initialize normal Initiative.
Ambush grants no universal Hit or Damage bonus beyond explicit rules.

CURRENT-ACTOR NARRATION LOCK
After mechanics commit, prose may describe only actions/movement already resolved for the Current Actor plus passive consequences of those resolved effects.
A different living combatant may not take fresh voluntary movement, attacks, dodges, charges, retreats or other actions during another actor's Turn unless an explicit Reaction/Interrupt/Ongoing mechanic authorizes it.
Physical momentum already created by a resolved effect may continue narratively only when it does not create an extra mechanical action.

PC ACTION SCOPE
A declared attack or Skill authorizes only that action and its written movement component. It never adds an approach, posture change, reload/nock, looting, inspection or repositioning for Alaric afterwards unless the user declared it; otherwise his previous position, posture and held items are copied forward unchanged.

rpg_compile.mode: condensed: initiative, ambush, actor/narration lock, PC ACTION SCOPE

25.content:
COMBAT XP FORMULA
Base XP = defeated target Level*10.
Rank-gap modifier versus player's Rank at encounter start: same x1; +1 x2; +2 x4; +3+ x8; -1 x0.5; -2 or lower x0.25.
Target type: Normal x1; Elite x1.5; Boss x2.5.
Final target XP = round(Base XP * Rank-gap * Target-type).

DEFEAT-XP LOCK
During Combat Initialization calculate each actual hostile's Final target XP ONCE from:
- that target's locked Level;
- that target's locked Rank;
- that target's locked Normal/Elite/Boss type;
- Alaric's Rank at encounter start.
Store it as FIXED `DefeatXP` for that encounter.
ACTIVE Combat never guesses, recalculates from prose, or changes DefeatXP.
On an eligible defeat, add exactly that locked DefeatXP once to Pending Combat XP.
Escaped targets contribute 0.

ELIGIBLE DEFEAT
Award eligibility exists when a real independent opponent/Monster is decisively defeated through death, explicit nonlethal incapacitation or finalized surrender/defeat. A legitimate wild-Monster hunt may qualify even if the Monster did not attack first.
No XP for helpless/captive/domesticated farming, already-defeated bodies, artificial repeat targets, or non-encounters without meaningful independent opposition.

PENDING-ONLY LOCK
During ACTIVE Combat record each eligible defeated target once into Pending Combat XP using its locked DefeatXP, but NEVER add it to persistent XP and NEVER trigger Level-Up while any hostile combatant remains active.
The terminal Combat End Loop verifies target uniqueness and awards the whole Pending total exactly once.

QUEST XP
Quest Base XP = Recommended Level*10. Minor/routine x1.5; Standard x2; Dangerous x3; Major/Dungeon/major objective x5. Quest XP is separate from Combat XP unless the Quest explicitly replaces it.

rpg_compile.mode: WI #12 verbatim; DefeatXP formula condensed into START/PENDING

26.content:
COMBAT INITIALIZATION LOOP — COMPLETE LOCK BEFORE PROSE
Run silently. Maximum two passes: CALCULATE -> AUDIT/REPAIR -> FINAL VERIFY. Never reroll during audit.

1. DETECT
Confirm hostile commitment under the Combat Phase Gate. If absent: remain INACTIVE; stop.

2. FREEZE SCENE
Lock every actual combatant, relevant Range Bands, terrain/LoS/cover, held/equipped items, current HP/MP/STA/ammo and the triggering hostile action.
Mere observers are not combatants. Do not invent exact meter distances.

3. ASSIGN STABLE IDs
Examples: Alaric, Boar#1, Wolf#1, Wolf#2. IDs persist for the encounter.

4. BUILD COMPLETE FIXED PROFILE FOR EVERY COMBATANT
Core-stat character FIXED fields:
ID | Level | Rank | Class/Evolution | STR VIT AGI INT PER WIL | MaxHP MaxMP MaxSTA | ATK MATK | Base/TOTAL DEF MDEF | Base Hit | Crit | Initiative | combat-relevant Gear | exact Action Library.

ATK = equipped Gear ATK + explicit ATK bonuses.
MATK = equipped Gear MATK + explicit MATK bonuses.
Never add STR/AGI/INT/PER or another Core Stat directly to ATK/MATK unless an explicit mechanic says so; Stats enter attacks through the locked action's written Scaling.

Direct-stat Monster FIXED fields:
ID | species/body-plan | Level | Rank | Normal/Elite/Boss | MaxHP | ATK | DEF | MDEF | Hit | Initiative | Attack Type | Attack Range Band | Crit:none unless explicitly authored | explicit authored Traits/actions only | DefeatXP.
Generic Monsters NEVER gain Human Core Stats, MP/STA, Character Crit, Classes, Skill Proficiency, Gear or invented Traits/Skills merely from appearance/prose.
There is no generic Monster Movement stat; normal movement is the universal adjacent-one-band rule.

5. BUILD CURRENT STATE
Current HP/MP/STA, ammo, held/equipped state, current total defenses/power after explicit effects, relevant pairwise Range Bands, terrain/cover/LoS state, statuses/barriers/temporary modifiers, Defeated/Escaped flags, Pending Combat XP.

6. LOCK ACTION LIBRARY
Copy exact canonical action formulas/effects currently available to each combatant.
Do not paraphrase them into altered mechanics.
For generic direct-stat natural attack: Raw=ATK, Base Hit=Hit, maximum Range=profile Range Band, Crit:none, no MP/STA cost.

7. LOCK DEFEAT XP
For each actual hostile, calculate DefeatXP once from its locked Level/Rank/type and Alaric's Rank at encounter start using the Combat XP Formula.
Store DefeatXP inside FIXED. ACTIVE/END use this locked value; never improvise a reward later.

8. TRIGGER ACTION / TARGET
True successful Ambush -> resolve Opening Action under Ambush rules (eligible attacks +25 percentage points Crit Chance; no Hit or Damage bonus; then normal Initiative).
Otherwise store the exact hostile trigger as Pending; do not resolve it yet.
If Alaric omitted a target and exactly one valid hostile exists, that sole hostile may be locked as target.
If multiple valid hostiles exist and Alaric did not choose one, stop at the target-choice boundary before cost/RNG.

9. INITIATIVE
Calculate once under Core; lock Turn Order. Set Round1 and highest legal Current Actor only after profile audit passes.

10. AUDIT / FINAL VERIFY
Independently recompute all derived PC values, ATK/MATK from Gear+explicit bonuses only, total DEF/MDEF, Monster direct fields from the chosen anchor/level when generated, DefeatXP, action formulas, resources<=max, Range Bands and Initiative.
Range listed on an action is its MAXIMUM band: LONG reaches LONG/MEDIUM/SHORT/ENGAGED; MEDIUM reaches MEDIUM/SHORT/ENGAGED; SHORT reaches SHORT/ENGAGED; ENGAGED reaches ENGAGED only.
Normal movement may traverse only one adjacent step: LONG<->MEDIUM<->SHORT<->ENGAGED.
Keep all attack scaling and damage intermediates at full precision; only final positive damage is rounded.
Repair mismatch once; verify once.

11. COMMIT COMPLETE ENCOUNTER SNAPSHOT BEFORE PROSE
Combat does not become safely ACTIVE until the complete FIXED profiles/Action Libraries plus CURRENT encounter state, Turn Order, Round, Current Actor, Pending action and phase are preserved in recoverable authoritative context.
Use whatever persistent state/presentation mechanism the active host already provides; Avereth does not prescribe tags, envelope, order, Markdown, or a second tracker.
If the host cannot store an arbitrary required field, keep that field recoverable in the response's ordinary visible mechanical state rather than omitting it.
Only after successful snapshot commit set semantic phase ACTIVE and resolve legal Turns.
Narration may describe only committed mechanical outcomes.

27.content:
ACTIVE COMBAT TURN TRANSACTION LOOP
Run silently. Maximum two passes: CALCULATE -> AUDIT/REPAIR -> FINAL VERIFY. Never reroll valid rolls.

0. COPY-FORWARD / SNAPSHOT INTEGRITY LOCK
Load the previous authoritative encounter snapshot.
Copy every FIXED profile, locked Action Library and locked DefeatXP exactly.
Do not regenerate Level, MaxHP, ATK/DEF/MDEF/Hit/Init, individual variation, Skills, Traits, action formulas or DefeatXP from species/prose.
CURRENT changes only by explicit deltas.
If any mechanically required FIXED field is missing and cannot be copied verbatim from an earlier explicit authoritative snapshot still present in context, STOP mechanical resolution.
Do not guess or reconstruct it. Spend/roll/change nothing, preserve Current Actor/phase, and surface a private state-integrity notice through the active presentation.

1. ACTOR
Read Round and Current Actor before interpreting the new action.
- Alaric Current Actor: use only the user's declared action, subject to the sole-hostile target default below.
- NPC/Monster Current Actor: choose only among its locked legal actions according to its own knowledge, goals, behavior and current state.

2. NPC DECISION LOCK — CAUSALITY BEFORE PLAYER CONVENIENCE
For an NPC/Monster Turn, choose and lock its legal action plus ordinary adjacent-one-band movement BEFORE evaluating whether that choice preserves or invalidates Alaric's pending action.
Never invent reduced movement, hesitation, restraint, favorable positioning, tactical stupidity, carrying penalties or another new rule merely to keep Alaric's pending action legal.
A combatant may voluntarily move less than one band only when that choice follows from its own established behavior/state, not from protecting a desired player outcome.

3. TARGET RESOLUTION
If exactly ONE valid hostile target exists and Alaric declares an offensive action without naming a target, use that sole hostile.
If TWO OR MORE valid hostile targets exist and no target was chosen, stop before cost/ammo/RNG/effect. Keep Alaric Current Actor.

4. HARD LEGALITY GATE
Validate actor active/alive; target; exact action; weapon/held requirements; current MP/STA; ammo; start Range Band; LoS; legal band movement; post-movement Range Band.
The action's listed Range is its MAXIMUM band:
LONG -> ENGAGED/SHORT/MEDIUM/LONG;
MEDIUM -> ENGAGED/SHORT/MEDIUM;
SHORT -> ENGAGED/SHORT;
ENGAGED -> ENGAGED only.
If Alaric's declared/pending action fails any hard requirement: spend NOTHING, consume NO ammo, make NO roll, deal NO effect, do NOT degrade/substitute, do NOT advance Turn. Keep Alaric Current Actor and return at the decision boundary.

5. MOVEMENT / RANGE — ADJACENCY LOCK
Every normal combatant may shift at most one adjacent Range Band on its Turn.
Only legal ordinary transitions: ENGAGED<->SHORT, SHORT<->MEDIUM, MEDIUM<->LONG.
An explicit locked Skill/Trait may grant/prevent/alter band movement.
Do not track or invent exact meters.
Narrative words like charge/rush/pounce/sprint grant no extra band shift by themselves.

6. COMMIT COST
Only after full legality: apply committed movement, MP/STA and physical ammo/consumable cost exactly once.
0 MP/STA creates NO automatic exhaustion/status/penalty; it only prevents unaffordable actions.

7. HIT
Core-stat Base Hit = 70 + PER*0.50.
Direct-stat Monster Base Hit = locked Hit.
Final Hit = Base Hit + explicit action/attacker modifiers - explicit avoidance/cover modifiers +/- established situational modifiers; clamp uncertain attacks 20%-95%.
Roll one d100. <= Final Hit = hit.
ENGAGED/SHORT range, target size, low HP, charging or dramatic preference never auto-hit an active target.

8. CRIT
Only on a hit and only if profile uses Crit.
Character Crit = 5% + PER/10 percentage points unless explicit mechanics modify it.
Generic direct-stat Monster Crit:none.
Roll one d100 once.

9. RAW / DAMAGE — FULL PRECISION
Character Physical Raw = Skill Base + exact Stat Scaling + ATK.
Character Magical Raw = Skill Base + exact Stat Scaling + MATK.
Generic direct-stat natural attack Raw = ATK.
Character ATK/MATK come from equipped Gear + explicit bonuses only; never add Core Stats twice.
NEVER round individual scaling terms, the scaling sum, Raw, Modified Power, defense result, resistance result, variance result or crit result.
Damage order: Raw -> explicit Power modifiers -> proficiency -> buffs/debuffs -> Domain -> penetration/reduction -> applicable TOTAL DEF/MDEF [max(Power-Defense, Power*0.10)] -> Resistance/Weakness -> one variance 0.90-1.10 -> Crit x1.5 if eligible -> Final modifiers -> round ONCE -> Barrier -> HP.
Defense is always applied BEFORE variance: PostDEF = max(Modified Power - applicable TOTAL DEF/MDEF, Modified Power x0.10), then Resistance/Weakness, then variance.
Use TOTAL DEF/MDEF, including equipped Gear and explicit current effects.

10. MULTI-HIT / AOE
Follow exact locked action definition. Separate strikes use separate Hit/Crit/damage when the action says so.
Stop extra strikes against a dead target unless retarget/area rules explicitly continue.

11. DEFEAT / PENDING XP
HP0 = dead unless explicit mechanics say otherwise.
Record eligible defeated target once and add exactly its locked FIXED DefeatXP to Pending Combat XP.
Never calculate a new reward from prose at death time.
While Combat remains ACTIVE, persistent XP, Level, Free Stat Points and end-loot DO NOT change.
Escaped target contributes 0.

12. ADVANCE
If hostiles remain active: advance Current Actor / Round exactly once, resolving NPC Turns automatically until Alaric is Current Actor or Combat becomes terminal.
If no hostile remains active: route immediately to Combat End Loop in the SAME response; do not output an intermediate ACTIVE state that awards XP early.

13. AUDIT / VERIFY
Recompute from the same locked inputs and same rolls: actor/target; legality; resource/ammo deltas; adjacent band movement/range; Hit; Crit; full-precision Raw; ATK/MATK source; TOTAL defense; variance; final damage; HP/status; locked DefeatXP/Pending XP; next actor/round.
Repair mismatch once. Verify once. Never reroll.

14. COMMIT SNAPSHOT THEN NARRATE
Preserve the complete recoverable FIXED+CURRENT encounter snapshot after applying deltas.
If the active host cannot store an arbitrary required combat field, retain it in ordinary visible mechanical state rather than dropping/reconstructing it.
Avereth prescribes semantic facts only, not host formatting.
Generate prose only after commit.
During a combatant's Turn, prose may not give another living combatant fresh voluntary movement/action unless an explicit Reaction/Interrupt/Ongoing mechanic already resolved it.

28.content:
COMBAT END / XP / PERSISTENCE LOOP
Combat End runs only when the encounter is terminal: no hostile combatant remains active because all are Defeated, Escaped, or have a finalized surrender/non-hostile resolution.
Maximum two passes: CALCULATE -> AUDIT/REPAIR -> FINAL VERIFY.

1. TERMINAL LOCK
If any hostile remains active, STOP: Combat stays ACTIVE and NO persistent XP/Level/end-loot is awarded.

2. FINALIZE SETS
Lock Defeated and Escaped once. A target appears in only one final category.

3. VERIFY PENDING XP FROM LOCKED ENCOUNTER VALUES
Each eligible Defeated target contributes exactly its FIXED DefeatXP locked during Initialization, once.
Escaped targets contribute 0.
Remove duplicate target awards and restore any omitted eligible locked award.
Do NOT invent a new XP value, alter target Level/Rank/type, or recalculate from narrative impressions at Combat End.

4. XP COMMIT — ONCE
Old persistent XP + verified Pending. Only now may XP/Level notices appear.

5. LEVEL LOOP
WHILE XP >= XP_TO_NEXT for the current Level:
- subtract threshold (Level*100);
- Level +1;
- +5 Free Stat Points;
- apply Base-Class favored +1/+1 growth;
- recalculate maxima/derived values.
Do NOT refill current HP/MP/STA merely because maxima increased.

6. LOOT / CORPSE STATE
Determine only physically recoverable external loot/materials. Never auto-pick-up, harvest, equip, sell or convert to Coin.

7. PERSIST
Start from the previous complete persistent character/world state and apply only terminal deltas. Preserve Rank/Class/Skills/Proficiency/Gear/Coin/Inventory/Quests/documents/relationships unless an explicit resolved event changed them.

8. AUDIT / VERIFY
Check locked DefeatXP uniqueness, Pending sum, XP arithmetic, number of Level-ups, Stats/maxima, current HP/MP/STA numerators, ammo, inventory/coin/quests/documents and Defeated/Escaped sets. Repair once; verify once.

9. COMMIT END
Clear Pending Combat XP only after successful award. Persist semantic Combat INACTIVE state so ACTIVE routing stops.
The host may render that state however its normal presentation expects; Avereth defines no specific label syntax or envelope.

previous_changes_v1.20: Host-format independence strengthened: Avereth defines semantic state only and never prescribes tracker envelopes, tags, ordering, Markdown, or any host-specific representation.
Combat START must commit a complete recoverable FIXED/CURRENT encounter snapshot before prose; ACTIVE hard-stops instead of regenerating any missing locked field from species/prose.
Range Bands are explicitly maximum ranges and normal movement can only traverse one adjacent band per Turn: LONG<->MEDIUM<->SHORT<->ENGAGED.
Precision lock strengthened: no individual scaling term, scaling sum, Raw Power, defense result, resistance result, variance result, or crit result is rounded before final damage.
Each hostile locks DefeatXP at initialization from fixed Level/Rank/type and encounter-start player Rank; ACTIVE and END use that locked value rather than improvising rewards.
Combat prose is bound to Current Actor and committed effects; no other living combatant may take fresh voluntary movement/action during another actor's Turn without an explicit reaction/ongoing rule.
Character Creation completion response remains System-only; story time resumes only on the next user turn.
